title: Best One-and-Done Limited Series
intro: The limited series is the most efficient storytelling format on streaming - no filler episodes, no renewal anxiety, no waiting for an ending that may never arrive. These shows end. They commit to their story, they close it, and they leave. That discipline is rarer than it should be, and these are the ones that used it well.

picks.title: Chernobyl
picks.one_line: Craig Mazin's HBO reconstruction of the 1986 disaster is five hours of procedural horror about what happens when a system is built to deny reality - the most acclaimed limited series of the last decade.

picks.title: Baby Reindeer
picks.one_line: Richard Gadd's autobiographical stalker drama refuses the comfort of a clean victim - seven episodes that get more complicated and more honest with each one.

picks.title: Adolescence
picks.one_line: A four-episode single-take British drama about a 13-year-old murder suspect - technically audacious and emotionally devastating, with a performance in Episode 3 that demands a pause afterward.

picks.title: Delhi Crime
picks.one_line: Shefali Shah leads the police investigation into the 2012 Delhi bus assault - a BAFTA-winning procedural that treats its subject with more dignity than any journalistic account managed.

picks.title: The Staircase
picks.one_line: A novelist's wife is found dead at the bottom of a staircase and the trial lasts 16 years - Colin Firth navigates a man who is either grieving husband or calculating killer with deliberate ambiguity.

picks.title: Scoop
picks.one_line: The backstory of Emily Maitlis's Prince Andrew Newsnight interview - Gillian Anderson's portrayal of a journalist navigating access politics is the best work she's done since The Crown.

picks.title: Sharp Objects
picks.one_line: Gillian Flynn's Missouri Gothic limited series - eight episodes of Amy Adams unravelling in the town she escaped, directed by Jean-Marc Vallée in a style that makes every surface feel contaminated.

picks.title: The Watcher
picks.one_line: Ryan Murphy adapts a real New Jersey stalker case into a suburban nightmare that escalates into something stranger than the facts - not prestige, but compulsively watchable.

faq.q: What is the single best limited series to watch right now?
faq.a: Chernobyl, by near-universal agreement. Five hours, no padding, and a closing episode that recontextualises everything that came before. Adolescence is the more recent challenger - shorter, more visceral, technically remarkable - and the conversation between the two is worth having.

faq.q: What counts as a 'limited series' - does Delhi Crime Season 2 break it?
faq.a: For this list, 'limited' means the original story is told in a single closed season - a second season that tells a different case (like Delhi Crime S2) still qualifies the original. What disqualifies a show is a cliffhanger ending designed to force renewal, which none of these do.
